children: B. Riley Securities is sticking with bullish ratings on IonQ

ahead of Quantum World Congress, betting that a shift in government policy from pure research toward commercialization could open a more meaningful revenue path for the quantum-computing sector. The firm maintained Buy ratings with price targets of $100 for IonQ, $40 for D-Wave and $35 for Rigetti.
The key catalyst is not a new contract or funding award, but the tone of the September 23-25 conference.

B. Riley analyst Craig Ellis highlighted the Department of Energy's From Lab to Market session as a sign that federal policy may increasingly focus on moving quantum technologies into commercial applications. The event will also include a two-hour National Quantum Updates session featuring more than 10 governments, alongside participation from the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. Microsoft and IBM are scheduled to deliver back-to-back keynotes.
That broader government presence matters because quantum companies still depend heavily on research funding, pilot programs and early-stage customer adoption.

For investors, the question is whether the conference produces evidence that public support is evolving into actual deployments, procurement programs or commercial partnerships. B. Riley's thesis is sector-wide: stronger government involvement could expand the long-term opportunity for quantum-computing companies.
The bullish call still has important gaps. The report does not provide fresh revenue forecasts, cash-flow estimates, technical milestones or new valuation work explaining the three price targets.

Quantum World Congress is more important as a validation event than an earnings catalyst. Investors should watch for new government programs, procurement commitments, commercial partnerships and clearer timelines for real-world deployment. Any concrete lab-to-market announcements would strengthen the case that quantum spending is moving beyond experimentation. Without them, the stocks remain heavily dependent on long-term expectations rather than near-term financial evidence.

title: B. Riley Sees Major Catalyst for Quantum Stocks
